gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Electrical Safety First's July 2026 lab test failed all 14 travel adaptors it bought from AliExpress, eBay, Amazon Marketplace and TikTok Shop, or that on 6 of the 8 universal adaptors more than one set of plug pins could be exposed and live at the same time.
standout_why: I compared it against packandporter.com (states 'We have not tested this gear'), NBC Select (no lab measurements, only interviews and staff anecdotes), thefinerroute.com (picks are 'based on the makers' published specs… and buyer feedback') and the other top results. None of them gives a measured figure or a third-party safety-lab result. Their safety content stops at maker claims such as fuses and shutters.
decides: It supports the plain single-plug Type C adapter, such as the Ceptics CTU-9C ChatGPT showed, for a continental-Europe-only trip. That design has no spare pin sets that can become live. It also means a universal slider adapter like the Epicka TA-105S should come from a named brand and not from an anonymous marketplace seller. The test did not cover the named candidates, so it does not rank them against each other. I could not confirm either maker's interlock or shutter design because their pages failed to load.

findings.label: Electrical Safety First test of marketplace travel adaptors: overall pass rate
findings.source_title: 'Highly dangerous' travel adaptors found for sale to UK consumers (Irish News, PA)
findings.note: Electrical Safety First, a UK charity, bought 14 adaptors from AliExpress, eBay, Amazon Marketplace and TikTok Shop. Article dated 29 July 2026. The article gives no per-platform split, and the products were unbranded marketplace units, not the candidates.

findings.source_title: 'Highly dangerous' travel adaptors found for sale to UK consumers (Irish News, PA)
findings.note: Same Electrical Safety First test. All 8 universal units also failed the pin dimension and mechanical strength requirements.

findings.label: Flammability test failures
findings.source_title: 'Highly dangerous' travel adaptors found for sale to UK consumers (Irish News, PA)
findings.note: The article says an external specialist laboratory ran the tests but does not name it. The 6 basic adaptors also failed on missing covers or fuses, oversized pin holes, and accepting three-pin plugs without an earth connection.

findings.label: Teardown of a $9.26 universal adapter: unused plug sets live
findings.value: With any one of the 3 plug sets in a socket, the other 2 were live; a resistance check showed all three were linked; pins were not live when fully retracted
findings.source_title: Dissecting A Lethal Universal Travel Adapter (Hackaday, Maya Posch, 2026-08-30)
findings.note: The teardown is by the YouTuber Brainiac 75, reported by Hackaday. The adapter's USB ports claim 5 V 2.1 A but have no hard cut-off. Hackaday gives no measured voltage. The article does not identify the brand.
